title: Tookoolito, C. F. Hall, and Ebierbing
creator: Charles Parsons, W. S. L. Jewett, H. L. Stephens, Granville Perkins, S. Eytinge, after a photograph
description: Engraved frontispiece group portrait of the Inuit couple Tookoolito and Ebierbing standing with Charles Francis Hall between them, all in fur winter dress. It served as the frontispiece to Hall's 1864 narrative of his first Arctic expedition.

title: Ascent of an Iceberg
creator: Charles Parsons and others, after C. F. Hall
description: A lone figure climbs the sloping face of a large iceberg using a boat-hook as an improvised alpenstock, with a small boat waiting below. Hall describes reaching the summit of a berg during the George Henry's outward voyage and injuring his foot descending it.

title: Portrait of Kudlago
creator: Charles Parsons and others, after C. F. Hall
description: Small oval engraved portrait of Kudlago, the Inuit man recruited in Cumberland Sound as a guide and interpreter for Hall's expedition, who died of illness aboard the George Henry before reaching home.

title: Burial of Kudlago
creator: Charles Parsons and others, after C. F. Hall
description: The crew of the George Henry gathered on deck for the sea-burial of Kudlago, whose body is being committed to the water wrapped in canvas. Hall recorded the funeral as a solemn shipboard occasion witnessed by the whole company.

title: Kudlago's Monument
creator: Charles Parsons and others, after C. F. Hall
description: An iceberg viewed from the ship, described by Hall as a natural "monument of mountain size" that he likened to a memorial for Kudlago as the George Henry sailed on after the burial.

title: Greenland Currency
creator: unidentified engraver, after a specimen collected by the author
description: Facsimile engraving of a Danish trade note ("6 Skilling Rigsmont") used as currency at the Greenland trading posts, reproducing the printed Danish text and a handwritten endorsement. Hall describes an Inuit crewman being given such a note in a shipboard trading joke.

title: Greenland Woman and Child
creator: facsimile after a woodcut by an unidentified Esquimaux artist
description: Standing portrait of a Greenland Inuit woman in fur boots and parka carrying a child in the hood on her back, captioned as a facsimile of a woodcut actually cut by an Inuit engraver. Hall presents it as evidence of Inuit artistic skill.

title: Festival on the Birthday of the King of Denmark
creator: Charles Parsons and others, after C. F. Hall
description: A dog-sledge procession and gathered crowd celebrating the Danish king's birthday at a Greenland settlement, rendered as a full-page plate. The scene shows sledge teams lined up before spectators at the trading post.

title: Dance on Board the George Henry
creator: Charles Parsons and others, after C. F. Hall
description: Sailors and Greenland women dancing together on the deck of the whaling barque George Henry, with onlookers crowded around the rail. Hall recounts joining the dance himself despite his self-professed clumsiness.

title: Esquimaux Feat -- A Summerset
creator: Charles Parsons and others, after C. F. Hall
description: A small coastal view showing the setting where an Inuit man, seated in his kayak, performed repeated somersaults in the water without capsizing or even fully wetting himself, a feat of skill Hall describes as rare and demanding.

title: Belted Iceberg
creator: Charles Parsons and others, after C. F. Hall
description: A tall iceberg banded with a dark horizontal stripe of embedded debris, rendered as a full-page plate among Hall's series of iceberg studies made while the ship lay amid the ice.

title: Gothic Iceberg
creator: Charles Parsons and others, after C. F. Hall
description: An iceberg carved by melting into pointed, arch-like forms that Hall compares to Gothic architectural ornament, with pinnacles and hollows resembling a ruined structure.

title: Distorted Moon
creator: Charles Parsons and others, after C. F. Hall
description: An atmospheric plate depicting the moon's disc distorted by refraction low over the ice horizon, part of Hall's record of unusual optical phenomena seen from the ship among the icebergs.

title: My Last Sight of the Runaways
creator: Charles Parsons and others, after C. F. Hall
description: A small boat under sail pulling away across open water, watched from the ship. The plate illustrates two crewmen's escape by boat toward Hudson's Bay Company posts, the last Hall saw of them as they departed.

title: Iceberg and Kia
creator: Charles Parsons and others, after C. F. Hall
description: A small vignette showing an Inuit kayak (kia) paddling near a low iceberg, illustrating the approach to the anchorage as the ship neared its harbour after a long day's sailing.

title: Pipe-Sketch -- Clark's Harbour
creator: Charles Parsons and others, after C. F. Hall
description: A small vignette sketch made at Clark's Harbour in the Frobisher Bay region, one of Hall's informal on-the-spot drawings worked up as a wood engraving.

title: Sterry's Tower
creator: Charles Parsons and others, after C. F. Hall
description: A tall, tower-like pillar of rock or ice named for Sterry, the carpenter of the George Henry, standing near the ship's route through the Frobisher Bay region.

title: Frobisher Bay and Grinnell Glacier
creator: Charles Parsons and others, after C. F. Hall
description: A panoramic full-page plate looking across Frobisher Bay toward Kodlunarn Island and the Grinnell Glacier, showing the ice-covered highlands behind the anchorage where Hall was gathering Inuit testimony about Frobisher's sixteenth-century voyages.

title: Esquimaux Chart, Drawn by Koojesse
creator: Koojesse
description: A hand-drawn chart of Frobisher Bay ("Tin-nu-jok-ping-oo-se-ong") and Cumberland Sound (Kin-gaite) made by the Inuit guide Koojesse at Rescue Harbour in 1860 for C. F. Hall, showing the coastline, islands, and Hudson Strait. Hall reproduced it to demonstrate the accuracy of Inuit geographic knowledge.

title: Wreck of the Rescue and of the Expedition Boat
creator: Charles Parsons and others, after C. F. Hall
description: A dramatic full-page plate of ice-wrecked timbers and a stranded hull, showing the schooner Rescue and one of the expedition's boats destroyed by pack ice near Rescue Harbour.

title: The Aurora, Nov. 23, 1860
creator: Charles Parsons and others, after C. F. Hall
description: A full-page plate of the northern lights in bright vertical bands over the winter camp, one of two aurora studies Hall had engraved from sketches made at Field Bay.

title: Aurora, December 17, 1860
creator: Charles Parsons and others, after C. F. Hall
description: A second full-page aurora plate showing tall radiating streamers of light filling the sky, sketched six weeks after the first and engraved as its companion image.

title: Nikujar, the Boat-Steerer and Pilot
creator: Charles Parsons and others, after C. F. Hall
description: Small circular portrait of Nikujar, the Inuit woman who piloted a whaleboat through the channels of Frobisher Bay with her infant riding in the hood of her parka, described by Hall as a capital pilot who knew every inlet.

title: Bone Sledge-Runner
creator: Charles Parsons and others, after an implement collected by the author
description: A curved runner for an Inuit sledge, made of bone or ivory and shod for travel over snow and ice, drawn as a specimen among the implements Hall collected in the Frobisher Bay region.

title: Bear Hunt -- "Tapping the Jugular"
creator: Charles Parsons and others, after C. F. Hall
description: Inuit hunters and dogs surround a polar bear at bay on the ice, the climactic moment of a hunt Hall witnessed in which the bear was finally brought down after a long chase.

title: Kood-lin and Ik-ku-mer, the Stone Lamp and Fire of the Esquimaux
creator: Charles Parsons and others, after an implement collected by the author
description: A soapstone oil lamp and its wooden drying frame, the all-purpose Inuit lamp Hall describes as giving heat, light, and cooking fire during the long Arctic winter night.

title: Ek-ke-lu-yun, the White-Stone Salmon-Bait Used by Esquimaux
creator: Charles Parsons and others, after an implement collected by the author
description: A carved white-stone lure used by Inuit fishermen to attract salmon, drawn from a specimen Hall obtained; he notes it was made with exceptional craftsmanship.

title: The "George Henry" in Winter Quarters
creator: Charles Parsons and others, after C. F. Hall
description: The whaling barque George Henry frozen into her winter anchorage at Rescue Harbour, masts bare and hull banked by snow and ice, with figures on the surrounding shore.

title: The Dying Esquimaux -- Nukertou
creator: Charles Parsons and others, after C. F. Hall
description: An Inuit woman, Nukertou, lies gravely ill on a snow platform attended by Tookoolito; Hall recorded her death at this bedside and the mourning that followed among her people.

title: Storm-Bound -- Encampment on the Floe of Davis's Straits, January 12th and 13th, 1861
creator: Charles Parsons and others, after C. F. Hall
description: Travelers and sledge dogs huddled beside an ice hummock in driving snow, illustrating a two-day storm that trapped Hall's party on the sea ice of Davis Strait until a snow-house shelter could be built.

title: Head and Antlers of the Arctic Reindeer
creator: Charles Parsons and others, after a specimen collected by the author
description: A mounted reindeer head and antlers shown as a natural-history specimen, illustrating the caribou hunted by Hall's Inuit companions for food and skins.

title: Sealing in the Winter
creator: Charles Parsons and others, after C. F. Hall
description: A full-page plate of a lone Inuit hunter standing motionless over a seal's breathing-hole, harpoon raised, waiting in the cold for the animal to surface -- the patient method of winter sealing Hall describes in detail.

title: Barbekark Killing the Reindeer
creator: Charles Parsons and others, after C. F. Hall
description: The ship's Greenland dog Barbekark seizing a reindeer by the throat on the open tundra, the scene of a hunt in which the dog ran down and killed a deer some two miles from the ship.

title: The Lost Found -- Frozen Dead
creator: Charles Parsons and others, after C. F. Hall
description: Search party members stand around the frozen body of John Brown, a crewman who had wandered off and died of exposure; Hall describes the discovery and the men's grief at finding him.

title: Parhelia, or Mock Suns, Seen at Field Bay, March 14, 1861
creator: Charles Parsons and others, after C. F. Hall
description: A circular plate of a halo display around the sun with bright mock-sun images to either side, observed and sketched at Field Bay in March 1861 as an example of Arctic atmospheric optics.

title: An Esquimaux and His Seal Dog
creator: Charles Parsons and others, after C. F. Hall
description: A standing Inuit hunter with his sealing dog beside him, equipped for the hunt; Hall's text describes how the dog is trained to locate and mark a seal's breathing-hole beneath the snow.

title: Blind George and His Daughter
creator: Charles Parsons and others, after C. F. Hall
description: Blind George, an Inuit man known to the crew as Paulooyer and blinded by snow-blindness, stands with his daughter who guided him; Hall describes him as living with the Inuit and still able to work his way carefully across the ice.

title: Igloos, or Snow Village, at Oopungnewing
creator: Charles Parsons and others, after C. F. Hall
description: A sideways full-page plate of a cluster of snow-block igloos forming a winter village at Oopungnewing, with figures and sledge dogs among the domed houses on the ice.

title: Ood-loo, or Woman's Knife
creator: after an implement collected by the author
description: A fan-shaped Inuit woman's knife of bone and iron, engraved at one-third the size of the original specimen; Hall notes it served an Inuit woman as knife, hatchet, scraper, and shears in one tool.

title: Old Ookijoxy Ninoo Narrating the Traditions of Her People
creator: Charles Parsons and others, after C. F. Hall
description: The elderly Ookijoxy Ninoo reclines in her tupic at Cooper's Island near Rescue Harbour, recounting to Hall through Tookoolito's interpreting the oral traditions of white men who had come to the country many generations before -- testimony that helped confirm the Frobisher expeditions of 1576-78 from Inuit memory alone.
